prompt:
Here is a problem from another field that shares the underlying structure of the research question below, with notes on how that field investigates it.

<parallel>
Field: Historical linguistics (lexical resistance to sound change)
Problem: Why do a few words escape a sound change that regularly applies to every instance of the same phoneme in a language?
How it is studied: Researchers reconstruct proto-forms with the comparative method and check which lexical items deviate from the regular correspondences. Corpus and frequency analyses test whether high-frequency or morphologically fused words resist change more often. Bayesian phylogenetic and lexical-diffusion models are fit to cognate data across related languages to separate stochastic drift from word-specific factors.
</parallel>

Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Regular-correspondence baseline with exception mining
ideas.description: Using paired single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq before and after drug exposure, first define the dominant 'regular' response shared by most dying cells, as a comparative method defines regular sound correspondences. Then isolate the survivors whose profiles deviate from that rule and reconstruct their pre-treatment state, testing whether the deviation was already present before drug exposure.

ideas.title: Frequency-stratified test of survival-linked features
ideas.description: As corpus studies test whether high-frequency or morphologically fused words resist change, measure whether survivors are enriched for high-expression, high-copy-number, or heterochromatin-locked loci, using frequency-matched gene sets as controls. A pooled CRISPR screen with guide abundance tracked across treatment can show whether these features predict survival beyond chance.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage phylogenetics to separate heritable from stochastic tolerance
ideas.description: Label founder cells with heritable lentiviral barcodes, reconstruct clonal trees from the sequenced barcodes, and fit Bayesian phylogenetic models to ask whether drug survival is clade-correlated (heritable, cell-intrinsic) or scattered across the tree (stochastic drift). This mirrors separating shared inheritance from random noise in cognate-based phylogenies.

ideas.title: Lexical-diffusion-style fitting of persister emergence over time
ideas.description: Track the fraction of surviving cells across repeated drug pulses and fit S-curve or spread models, as lexical-diffusion studies do for words changing across speakers. Adding spatial imaging in 3D culture lets the lab test whether tolerant states propagate between neighboring cells (contagion-like diffusion) or arise independently in each cell.

ideas.title: Cross-cell-line comparison of survival signatures as cognates
ideas.description: Compare survival programs across several cancer cell lines or patient-derived models, treating each as a related language and each shared survival gene program as a cognate. Phylogenetic-style analysis then identifies conserved, lineage-independent survival mechanisms versus lineage-specific ones, which can be checked by reprogramming a candidate gene in a naive line.
